chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah took a Covenant upon the Momin (to have patience) such that his words would not be accepted as true and he would not avenge himself against his enemy. No Momin will find any satisfaction for his soul except through its disgrace (before his own conscience), for every Momin is harnessed (bridled from his worldly desires).

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: The Momin — the true, committed believer
key_terms.عَدُوِّهِ: His enemy — the adversary from whom the believer refrains from taking revenge
key_terms.فَضِيحَتِهَا: Its disgrace / its exposure — the humbling of the soul before one's own conscience
key_terms.مَقَالَتُهُ: His words / his statement — referring to the believer's speech being disbelieved or dismissed
key_terms.مُلْجَمٌ: Harnessed / bridled — one fitted with a bridle, here a metaphor for the believer's complete restraint of worldly and egoic desires
key_terms.مِيثَاقَ: Covenant / solemn pledge — the binding divine compact Allah has imposed upon the believer
key_terms.يَشْفِي نَفْسَهُ: To satisfy / to heal his soul — to find comfort or relief for the nafs
key_terms.يَنْتَصِفَ: To avenge / to exact full retribution — the act of taking equal revenge from an enemy

ai.seo_question: What covenant has Allah taken upon every believer (Momin) regarding patience and self-restraint according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) describes a divine Covenant that Allah has imposed upon every true believer: that he will endure the trial of not being believed, will refrain from fully avenging himself against his enemies, and will find no comfort for his nafs except by holding it to account and exposing its faults. The concluding image of the Momin as 'harnessed' (muljam) conveys that restraint of the soul and its desires is the very hallmark of genuine faith.
